History and Development of the Company
MMA.INC
is the community platform for combat sports. Running and cycling have Strava. Fitness has Mindbody and ClassPass. Hiking has AllTrails.
We believe combat sports has never had a platform of its own, and that is what we have built.
Our
mission is to convert the more than 700 million martial arts fans around the world into participants (source: TKO Group Holdings, Inc.,
“Paramount and UFC Expand Partnership to Canada Beginning in 2027”, June 4, 2026). The UFC monetizes viewership. We monetize
participation.
We
have spent nine years putting the pieces together. From 2017 we built credibility inside the sport through the Warrior Training Program.
Between 2023 and 2024 we acquired the assets we could not build overnight, being MixedMartialArts.com, Hype and BJJLink, and established
our relationship with UFC GYM. Over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 we brought those assets together into one platform with one user journey.
Our focus now is monetizing the network we have already built.
Our
business is built around four products:
●
BJJLink:
our gym management and payments software for martial arts academies, covering memberships,
billing, class scheduling, attendance, point of sale and communication with students.
●
Warrior
Training Program: our 20 week program for people taking their first step into martial
arts, delivered through trainalta.com, licensed to partner gyms and run across UFC GYM locations.
●
MixedMartialArts.com:
one of the original domains in the sport and home of The Underground forum, which we soft
relaunched in July 2026.
●
XP
Passport: one identity and one record for every athlete, covering belts, fights, training
and gear, which we soft launched in July 2026 on a freemium basis.
As
at September 30, 2026, 15,408 academies were published on our platform, 1,148 of them were verified and 400 were paying. There were 120,048
registered students on the platform, 32,583 monthly active users in September 2026 and around 97,195 check ins. Payments processed through
the platform were US$2.11 million in September 2026, an annualized rate of US$25.4 million. Across all MMA.INC assets we have more than
5 million social media followers and around 680,000 user profiles.
We
define these metrics as follows. Published academies and user profiles are the academy and user profiles created across all assets owned
by MMA.INC and consolidated into our master database. Verified academies are published academies whose owner has taken control of their
profile. Paying academies are academies on an active paid subscription. Registered students are individual student records created on
the platform by academies or by students themselves. Monthly active users are unique users active in the relevant month across our app,
our kiosks in the gym and our admin interfaces. Check ins are attendance events recorded through the platform. Payment volume is the
gross value of payments processed through the platform, and the annualized figure annualizes recent monthly volume. Social media followers
are the cumulative total of followers across all MMA.INC assets since each asset started. Published academies, user profiles, registered
students and social media followers do not mean those academies or users are currently active or training, and payment volume is not
Company revenue. Our metrics may differ from similarly named metrics used by other companies.
During
fiscal 2026 our principal activities were licensing the Warrior Training Program to partner gyms, including UFC GYM locations, and providing
BJJLink software and payment services to martial arts academies. For the Warrior Training Program we provide the program, the syllabus,
marketing, payments and outsourced sales and customer service, and the partner gym delivers the training. The Warrior Training Program
remained our largest source of revenue during the year.
Business
developments during fiscal 2026 and first quarter of fiscal 2027
In
July 2025, the Company expanded its technology partnership with UFC Gym Group, with BJJLink.com selected as the official software platform
for UFC Gym’s new Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ) franchise studios. Under the multi-year software as a service (“SaaS”)
agreement, BJJLink will power the rollout and provide an all-in-one system for scheduling, billing, and member engagement.
In
July 2025, we terminated our US$2 million revolving loan agreement with Bowery Consulting Group Inc. The US$550,000 drawn under the facility
had been repaid in full, together with interest, before June 30, 2025.
In
July 2025, Laura Sanko joined the Board of Directors. Laura Sanko brings a wealth of expertise and passion to the Company’s Board
of Directors. As a trailblazing UFC commentator, Sanko made history as the first female color commentator in the modern UFC era, debuting
at UFC Fight Night in February 2023. Her insightful analysis, deep technical understanding of mixed martial arts and engaging presence
have made her a respected voice in the combat sports community.
In
July 2025, Aaron Links was appointed as our Chief Financial Officer.
Between
October and November 2025, we issued 975,000 Ordinary Shares in private placements at US$1.00 per share, raising US$975,000: 300,000
shares on October 3, 2025 to four investors under Regulation S, 250,000 shares on October 8, 2025 and 425,000 shares on November 13,
2025.
In
September 2025, Donald Trump Jr. was appointed as a Strategic Advisor under a 24-month agreement to assist with strategic alliances,
business development, and investor relations. In consideration for these services, an entity associated with Donald Trump Jr. received
options to purchase 1.5 million ordinary shares at US$0.001 per share, subject to a 12-month lock-up period and compliance with applicable
securities laws. The options have vested but have not been exercised as at the date of this annual report.
In
October 2025, we announced the development of our Web3 ecosystem and began building a rewards platform with the intention to enhance
community engagement through tokenized rewards.
Between
July and September 2025, all 5,677,139 prefunded warrants issued in our June 2025 public offering were exercised.
In
October 2025, we announced our development of our Web 3.0 ecosystem as part of our growth strategy. We commenced the building a rewards
platform to enhance community engagement through tokenized rewards, enabling users to “Get Paid to Train.”
In
December 2025, we entered into a strategic memorandum of understanding with World Liberty Financial to work together on developing the
MMA.INC token ecosystem and integrating the USD1 stablecoin as a means of payment across our platform.
In
December 2025, we completed a US$3 million private placement, consisting of 4,285,713 Series A Preference Shares with a 70c conversion
price, led by American Ventures LLC, with participation from Donald Trump Jr.
In
March 2026, we launched our gear and apparel revenue platform with Zebra Athletics, under which we intend to earn revenue on sales made
through our platform.
In
April 2026, the Warrior Training Program had its first international rollout with UFC GYM and went live across five UFC GYM sites in
Australia.
In
April 2026, we announced the intention to expand into law enforcement training with a program to be designed by John Kavanagh.
In
May 2026, we entered into an exclusive peptide partnership with Precision Peptide, under which we intend to earn revenue on sales made
to our community.
In
May 2026, we entered into a US$5 million unsecured revolving loan agreement with a private family office. Amounts drawn carry interest
at 12% per year, which is capitalized, and the facility has a 24 month term. The facility is not convertible and no warrants were issued
in connection with it. At October 30, 2026, this facility has not been drawn.
In
June 2026, we expanded BJJLink beyond gym management with the launch of an AI powered member acquisition platform that helps academies
find and sign up new students.
In
June 2026, we terminated our undrawn US$20 million equity line, which simplified our capital structure.
Between
January 1, 2026 and June 30, 2026, holders converted 3,071,428 Series A Preference Shares into Ordinary Shares on a one-for-one basis
(conversion price US$0.70 per share), leaving 1,214,285 Series A Preference Shares on issue at June 30, 2026. Between July 1, 2026 and
November 17, 2026, holders converted a further 357,143 Series A Preference Shares, so that 3,428,571 had been converted in total and
857,142 Series A Preference Shares remained on issue at November 17, 2026.
In
July 2026, we relaunched MixedMartialArts.com and launched XP Passport on a freemium basis. We have not yet enabled the monetization
layer and XP Passport does not currently generate revenue.

risks:
Summary
of Principal Risks
●
We
require substantial additional capital to fund operations; financing may not be available
on acceptable terms (or at all), which could dilute shareholders and constrain the business.
●
We
have a history of losses and expect operating expenses to increase; we may not achieve or
maintain profitability.
●
There
is a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on our ability to continue as a
going concern, and our auditor’s report includes an explanatory paragraph stating that
there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
●
Our
results are sensitive to discretionary consumer spending and broader macroeconomic conditions;
a downturn or reduced consumer demand could materially affect us.
●
Changes
in consumer tastes and trends in martial arts/fitness and content distribution could reduce
demand for our services and offerings.
●
We
rely heavily on technology (information systems, content distribution and payments); outages,
breakdowns, or cyber incidents could disrupt operations, harm our reputation, and trigger
regulatory obligations and costs.
●
A
breach or unauthorized disclosure of client/customer data—or attacks such as ransomware,
phishing, denial-of-service and related threats—could lead to litigation, fines, and
loss of business.
●
As
a forum/media platform operator, we face risks from unlawful or inappropriate user-generated
content and potential misuse of our platform, which can result in regulatory actions, litigation,
and brand harm.
●
Negative
social-media activity can rapidly damage our reputation and business and may expose us to
penalties if related laws are breached.
●
Our
brand and intellectual property are critical assets; infringement claims, inability to police
or protect rights (especially in some foreign jurisdictions), or third-party misuse could
harm our competitive position and results.
●
We
depend on partner gyms and key commercial relationships; their actions are outside our control,
termination/non-renewal, poor execution, or disputes may damage our brand and financial performance.
●
Our
model depends on attracting and retaining gym members; attrition, pricing pressure, or ineffective
marketing by us or partners could adversely affect revenues.
●
Expansion
and growth (including adding partner gyms) place strains on management, systems, and controls;
failure to scale effectively could harm performance.
●
We
face significant competition from multiple fitness and entertainment formats, including at-home/digital
offerings.
●
Operating
internationally exposes us to political, regulatory, operational, tax and infrastructure
risks, and challenges enforcing IP; these may restrict operations or increase costs.
●
Exchange-rate
movements can cause fluctuations in our reported results.
●
We
are subject to complex global tax requirements; permanent establishment, transfer pricing
and withholding/excise obligations could create additional liabilities.
●
If
we cannot recruit and retain key executives, coaches and professional fighters, our operating
efficiency and growth plans could suffer.
●
We
accept ACH/credit/debit payments; fee increases, software failures, fraud or loss of processing
capabilities could reduce revenue and harm operations.
●
Our
MMA “Final Fight Night” events are subject to regulation by government bodies
and state athletic commissions; non-compliance could lead to sanctions or suspension.
●
Our
digital asset initiatives, including the token and partnership arrangements announced during
the year, are subject to evolving regulation and may not succeed.
●
We
use artificial intelligence in parts of our business; its use carries operational and legal
risks and is subject to developing regulation.
●
We
are subject to government regulation in the jurisdictions in which we operate; changes in,
or non-compliance with, that regulation could increase our costs or restrict our operations.
●
As
a foreign private issuer, we incur higher compliance costs and rely on certain home-country
governance practices; inability to meet U.S. public-company requirements could result in
sanctions, litigation, or delisting.
●
We
have identified material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting and
are implementing remediation measures; if we do not remediate them or maintain effective
controls, our ability to produce accurate financial statements could be impaired.
●
Our
share price may be volatile due to performance, market conditions, analyst coverage, regulatory
changes, and sales by major holders; investors could lose part or all of their investment.
●
The
conversion price of our Series A Preference Shares may adjust downwards if we issue Ordinary
Shares at a lower price, which would increase the number of Ordinary Shares issuable on conversion.
●
The
number of Ordinary Shares outstanding has increased substantially and we expect to issue
further shares, which will dilute existing holders.
●
We
must satisfy the continued listing standards of the NYSE American and obtain its approval
before issuing additional Ordinary Shares.
●
We
do not expect to pay dividends for the foreseeable future; returns to shareholders may depend
on share-price appreciation.

summary should be read together with the full “Risk Factors” section; it does not contain all of the information that may

Risks
Related to Our Financial Position and Need for Additional Capital
We
will require substantial capital to finance our operations that may not be available to us on acceptable terms, or at all.

will require further funding to support our ongoing activities and operations. There can be no assurance that such funding will be available
on satisfactory terms or at all. Any inability to obtain funding will adversely affect our business and financial condition and consequently
our performance. We may seek to raise further funds through equity or debt financing, joint ventures or other means. There can be no
assurance that additional financing will be available when needed or, if available, that the terms of such financing will be favorable
to us, which may result in substantial dilution to our shareholders.
We
have incurred operating losses in the past, may incur operating losses in the future, and may not achieve or maintain profitability in
